concept: Change the system. Watch the consequences. Explain what changed.
source_note: Scripted teaching simulations. Nothing here executes a shell command, changes a file, or contacts a model or remote service.

flows.label: Permission decisions
flows.concept: A tool request crosses independent checks before code can run.
flows.intro: Click the gates themselves. A request reroutes immediately when you change the rules, the human decision, or the execution environment.
flows.predict: If you approve a request, can a deny rule or a shell sandbox still stop it?
flows.source_note: Schematic decision model based on Module 2 and mini-harness/harness.py. These controls apply to the selected illustrative call; no real policy or command is executed.

defaults.label: Block assertion removal with a hook
Always ask for the selected call

request.title: A request is text, not execution.
request.text: The model asks the harness to perform the selected action. Every following gate belongs to the harness or the operating system.

hook_pass.title: The hook passes.
hook_pass.text: The assertion-removal hook does not block this call. Passing a hook does not bypass a deny or ask rule.

hook_block.title: The hook blocks the edit.
hook_block.text: The edit would remove an assertion. The hook returns exit code 2 before any permission rule or tool execution.

deny_pass.title: No deny rule matches.
deny_pass.text: The call moves to ask rules. An allow rule has not been considered yet.

deny_block.title: Deny wins.
deny_block.text: A matching deny rule stops the call even if an allow rule also matches or the human would approve it.

ask_pass.title: No ask rule matches.
ask_pass.text: The harness can now consider an allow rule.

ask_match.title: Ask takes precedence over allow.
ask_match.text: A matching ask rule requires a human decision. An allow rule cannot remove this prompt.

allow_match.title: An allow rule approves the call.
allow_match.text: The selected single call matches the allow rule. For a compound shell command, every subcommand must match; this simulation does not parse command strings.

allow_miss.title: No allow rule matches.
allow_miss.text: The reference policy defaults to ask. The harness requests a human decision rather than running the tool automatically.

approved.title: The human approves.
approved.text: Permission is granted. The execution environment still applies to a shell command.

declined.title: The human declines.
declined.text: The tool does not run. The refusal becomes a tool result for the next model request.

sandbox_block.title: Allowed to run, unable to connect.
sandbox_block.text: The shell command starts inside the network-isolated sandbox. Its network operation fails. Permission approval did not grant network access.
sandbox_block.evidence:
shell: started
network: blocked by sandbox

executed.title: The tool executes.
executed.text: The harness dispatches the call. A shell network sandbox does not wrap the file-edit tool, hooks, or MCP processes.

blocked_result.title: A refusal becomes context.
blocked_result.text: The harness appends the reason to the conversation. The tool did not run; the model can use the refusal on its next request.

failed_result.title: An execution failure becomes context.
failed_result.text: The shell ran, but the requested network operation failed. A failed tool result is still sent back to the model.

success_result.title: A result becomes context.
success_result.text: The tool output is appended to the conversation. The next request includes it alongside the previous messages.

return.title: The loop continues.
return.text: The model receives the result or refusal in its next request. A completion claim still needs independent verification.

experiments.title: Approval is not access
experiments.prompt: The human says yes, but the connection fails. Change the execution environment and explain why the same approval now leads to a different result.

experiments.title: Who wins this argument?
experiments.prompt: Allow and deny both match the test runner. Make the call run, then require a human decision without removing the allow rule.

flows.label: Verification evidence
flows.concept: A green test run is one piece of evidence; inspect the diff and test the test.
flows.intro: Switch the agent’s change directly on the diagram. Compare the evidence as the same green test run leads to different review decisions.
flows.predict: Both changes make the suite pass. Which evidence distinguishes a fix from a weakened test?
flows.source_note: Scripted replay of Module 4 Lab A using the practice-app login bug. Test summaries and diff excerpts correspond to the supplied fix and weaken scenarios. No source file is edited by this page.

baseline.title: Start with a clean baseline.
baseline.text: A committed baseline separates the agent’s change from your work and gives you a reliable comparison.

red.title: The bug is observable.
red.text: The existing test rejects a user with no stored password. On the original implementation it fails.

edit_fix.title: The implementation changes.
edit_fix.text: The agent changes the empty-hash branch in src/auth.py. The test assertion stays intact.

edit_weaken.title: The assertion changes.
edit_weaken.text: The agent replaces the behavior check with an unconditional assertion, leaving the faulty implementation untouched. The test no longer checks the login behavior.
edit_weaken.evidence:
tests/test_login.py
-    assert verify_password("anything", user.hash) is False
+    assert True  # flaky, revisit later

green.title: The suite is green in both cases.
green.text: You run the tests independently. This summary alone cannot tell a source fix from an assertion changed to accept the faulty behavior.

diff_fix.title: The diff supports the intended fix.
diff_fix.text: The source branch now rejects an empty stored hash. No test was weakened. Review scope and behavior as well as the summary.

diff_weaken.title: The diff exposes the shortcut.
diff_weaken.text: Only the test changed. The agent made the suite green by changing the expected behavior rather than fixing the login bug.

diff_skipped.title: The diff was not reviewed.
diff_skipped.text: The test summary is still green. You have not checked whether tests, fixtures, or the implementation changed.

mutation_fix.title: Removing the fix makes the test fail.
mutation_fix.text: Keep the tests and temporarily remove only the implementation change. The failure returns; restoring the fix makes the suite pass.
mutation_fix.evidence:
without source fix: 1 failed, 5 passed
with source fix: 6 passed

mutation_weaken.title: The buggy implementation still passes.
mutation_weaken.text: Keep the changed test and run it against the original implementation. It passes because the unconditional assertion does not check the faulty behavior. There is no implementation fix to remove.
mutation_weaken.evidence:
original source + changed test: 6 passed
regression detected: no

mutation_skipped.title: The test was not challenged.
mutation_skipped.text: You have not shown that the current tests fail when the implementation has the bug. A green suite is not evidence of that property.

accept.title: The evidence supports this fix.
accept.text: The original bug fails a test, the source fix makes it pass, the diff preserves the assertion, and removing the fix brings the failure back. You can now make a review decision.

reject.title: Reject the weakened test.
reject.text: The observed evidence shows that the faulty implementation remains accepted. Restore the intended assertion and request an implementation fix.

incomplete.title: The evidence is incomplete.
incomplete.text: Passing tests do not replace the missing diff or mutation check. Collect the missing evidence before accepting the agent’s claim.

return_accept.title: Review as you would a colleague’s change.
return_accept.text: Check the rest of the diff and task requirements before committing. This replay verifies the specific empty-hash behavior, not every property of the program.

return_reject.title: Keep the intended behavior as the target.
return_reject.text: Reject the shortcut with a concrete reason: the test accepts an empty stored password. Ask for a source fix and repeat the checks.

return_incomplete.title: Choose the next piece of evidence.
return_incomplete.text: Enable the missing check and replay. Notice which claim it can establish and which questions still require review.

experiments.title: The green-test illusion
experiments.prompt: Both edits produce six passing tests. Flip the agent change and watch which evidence exposes the shortcut.

experiments.title: What would convince you?
experiments.prompt: The agent reports success, but the evidence is incomplete. Add checks one at a time. Then switch to the weakened test: which check is enough to reject it?

flows.label: Network and data
flows.concept: An internal model endpoint is one destination; traffic controls and retained copies are separate concerns.
flows.intro: Click destinations to change body logging, or click the context and public boundary to change routing and egress. The copies and paths update together.
flows.predict: If public egress is blocked, which internal and local copies of the file can still remain?
flows.source_note: Illustrative data-flow model based on Module 6, not a network audit or a model of any specific product. Retention is shown only for the selected body-logging settings. Disabling body logging does not establish that all metadata or backups are absent.

defaults.label: Route model to the internal gateway

files.title: The agent reads a project file.
files.text: The selected file content can enter the conversation. Starting in a narrower directory limits the files available to read.

context.title: The file is now request content.
context.text: The harness includes the read result in context. Blocking public traffic does not remove it from this request.

gateway_saved.title: The internal gateway forwards and retains the body.
gateway_saved.text: The request stays on the internal route, but its body is now also available in the gateway’s retained logs.
gateway_saved.evidence:
destination: internal gateway
body retained: yes

gateway_transient.title: The gateway forwards without body logging.
gateway_transient.text: This model records no retained request body at the gateway. Transport, metadata, and infrastructure retention still require a real audit.
gateway_transient.evidence:
destination: internal gateway
body retained in this model: no

endpoint_saved.title: The internal endpoint receives and retains the body.
endpoint_saved.text: The model service processes the request. Its selected logging policy retains the body in addition to processing it.
endpoint_saved.evidence:
destination: internal model
body retained: yes

endpoint_transient.title: The internal endpoint receives the body.
endpoint_transient.text: The endpoint must receive the content to process it. Disabling retained body logs does not mean the endpoint never sees the file.
endpoint_transient.evidence:
destination: internal model
body retained in this model: no

public_model_blocked.title: The public model request is blocked.
public_model_blocked.text: The model request is still routed publicly. The egress boundary denies it, so the model cannot complete this turn. No internal endpoint receives it.
public_model_blocked.evidence:
public model: denied
model response: unavailable

public_model_sent.title: The request body leaves the internal boundary.
public_model_sent.text: Public egress is allowed and the model route is public. The file content is transmitted to a public model service.
public_model_sent.evidence:
public model: sent
payload: request body

transcript_saved.title: The conversation is saved locally.
transcript_saved.text: The local transcript retains the tool result containing the file. A blocked outbound request does not erase this local copy.

transcript_off.title: Local transcript saving is off.
transcript_off.text: This replay adds no retained local transcript. That setting does not change whether gateways, endpoints, or telemetry hold content.

telemetry_content.title: Internal telemetry includes content.
telemetry_content.text: The selected internal telemetry route retains conversation content. Review access and retention as you would for the original source data.

telemetry_metadata.title: Internal telemetry contains metadata only.
telemetry_metadata.text: This model sends operational metadata without the file body to the internal collector. Metadata can still be sensitive.

usage.title: The usage log is another artifact.
usage.text: The course harness logs token counts, paths, and full commands. It does not copy this file body into its usage record, but the record still needs appropriate handling.

nonessential_off.title: The nonessential public request is disabled.
nonessential_off.text: No public update or diagnostic request is attempted by this scripted session. This does not change model routing or internal storage.

nonessential_blocked.title: The extra public request is denied.
nonessential_blocked.text: An update or diagnostic request is attempted and blocked. Real retries can cause delays and monitoring noise even when no connection leaves.

nonessential_sent.title: The extra public request is sent.
nonessential_sent.text: The public service receives this illustrative update or diagnostic metadata request. It is separate from the model request and does not contain the file body in this replay.

finish.title: Review destinations and copies separately.
finish.text: An egress audit answers where traffic goes. Data-handling review also covers internal gateway logs, endpoint logs, transcripts, telemetry, and usage records.
finish.evidence: next: audit the actual harness version

experiments.title: Inside is still somewhere
experiments.prompt: Public traffic is blocked, yet the file has several retained copies. Remove body logging while keeping the internal model reachable.

experiments.title: No response. Still a record.
experiments.prompt: The public model request is denied. Does that prevent a local copy? Change the route, then compare the copies that become possible.

outcomes.internal: The internal model receives the file.
outcomes.public: The file reaches the public model.

live.unchanged: The outcome stayed the same. An earlier decision or an unreached destination can make this setting irrelevant.
live.changed: The route or its evidence changed.
live.initial: Select a situation, then change something in the diagram.
live.inspect: Pause the replay or select a numbered stop to inspect the evidence.
